reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

description.narrative: ltpgtIn 2024, with funding from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF), UN Women on behalf of the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT), led the design and implementation of Wasil - an Inter-Agency Community Feedback Mechanism (CFM) established to strengthen collective Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPT). Launched in June 2025, Wasil (meaning “connection” in Arabic) is a unified, multi-sector system through which crisis-affected people - especially women and girls - can access trusted information, meaningful feedback channels, and safe referral pathways to lifesaving humanitarian assistance. In 2025 alone, the mechanism captured over 15,000 cases from Palestine, demonstrating significant community uptake and demand (64% of callers were women 11% were persons with disabilities or chronic conditions (including 877 women and girls) 22% from female-headed households 7% were pregnant or nursing women). The CFM is unique as an integrated system and referral mechanism. Through a single hotline, accessible via telephone, SMS, and WhatsApp, users can access up to date information on services such as food support, medical, legal aid, protection services, and cash support, receive referrals, and provide complaints and feedback about all humanitarian services available. The system avoids fragmented or parallel feedback channels by consolidating case intake, documentation, referral, follow-up, and closure within a harmonized inter-agency framework timely, coordinated and accountable responses. Through the Humanitarian Fund (HF), UN Women will strengthen the HCT-wide CFM through expanding the network of hotline operators, implemented with local partner Aisha Association for Woman and Child Protection (AISHA), increasing the pool of sector focal points for referrals, upgrading case management software, and reinforcing referral tracking protocols. Standardized response timelines, escalation pathways, and confirmation of case closure with beneficiaries will be applied to ensure transparent follow-up and accountability. The hotline will remain toll-free and confidential. Outreach efforts will prioritize women, persons with disabilities, elderly persons, and marginalized groups to ensure awareness and safe access. Operators will be trained on Prevention of Sexual Abuse and Exploitation, safe identification and referral, and survivor-centered approaches. For callers without direct access to services, operators will proactively coordinate with OCHA’s Humanitarian Service Directory, cluster focal points, and relevant partners to obtain updated information and revert to callers with verified guidance. Wasil will generate consolidated, anonymized data analysis products - including dashboards, thematic trend reports, and cluster-specific briefs - to inform humanitarian programming and coordination. Through UN Women’s role as co-chair of the Gender in Humanitarian Action, Working Group, and active membership in the national and Gaza AAP WG, key insights will be regularly shared with clusters and working groups to improve responsiveness, identify service gaps, and strengthen gender-responsive programming. To complement the strengthened CFM, the Project will also provide specialized protection case management and Cash for Protection (C4P) services through AISHA for high-risk individuals identified through the mechanism or other referral pathways. This includes displaced women and adolescent girls, women-headed households, women with disabilities, elderly women, and survivors of or those at risk of Gender Based Violence (GBV). Two installments of C4P will support urgent protection-related needs, reinforce case management outcomes, and help restore safety, dignity, and resilience. Through this integrated approach, the Project will reinforce collective accountability across the humanitarian response, transparent responsiveness, and trust between affected populations and humanitarian actors. ltbrgtlt/pgt
